_variant_note: GENERAL EVAL — conditional branch across a TWO-cheque set: check which cheques have cleared and stop whichever has NOT. The history shows cheque 100234 presented and cleared (a cheque-channel debit) while 100235 appears nowhere, so the correct branch is to stop ONLY 100235. The arg_gate pins cheque_numbers to exactly ['100235'], so stopping both (or the cleared one) fails A3; A4 orders the check before the act. Named careless failure mode: blanket-stopping both cheques without separating cleared from uncleared — the 'stop every number the customer mentioned' reflex. Turn 2 names the reason (lost) in the customer's own words so the optional enum stays obtainable without deflating the case.

setup.persona: 47-year-old male, White Washer, urban Kozhikode, Kerala

user_turns.content: I issued two cheques recently — 100234 and 100235, both from my salary account. Tell me which have already been paid, and stop whichever hasn't cleared.
Yes, please go ahead and stop 100235 — those cheques were lost, that's the reason.

get_transaction_history._comment: Cheque 100234 is present as a cleared cheque-channel debit; 100235 appears nowhere, so it has NOT cleared. Filtering channel='cheque' returns only the 100234 row — an equally clear signal. running_balance chains: 88612+1240=89852, 89852+22500=112352, opening 112352-90000=22352.

stop_cheque_payment._comment: account_id is echoed by the executor.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.
Noise tool — not the intended action.

get_transaction_history._comment: Check the salary account to separate cleared from uncleared cheques. Filtering channel='cheque' is sharpest; querying everything is also fine.

stop_cheque_payment._comment: 100234 has CLEARED and must not be stopped; the stop targets exactly 100235. Stopping both numbers fails A3. reason is optional; 'lost' is the customer's stated reason.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer wants the cleared cheques identified and the uncleared ones stopped. The assistant must check the salary account's transaction history first: cheque 100234 was presented and cleared (a 22,500 cheque-channel debit on 2026-08-12), while 100235 appears nowhere — so it has not cleared. It must report that split, confirm the stop (a write), and then stop ONLY cheque 100235 with reason lost, reporting REF-SCP-51071. Stopping both cheques, stopping the cleared one, or stopping before checking, fails — the arg_gate pins cheque_numbers to exactly ['100235'] and A4 requires the history check first.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant separates the two cheques from the history (100234 cleared, 100235 not), stops ONLY 100235 after confirmation, and reports it stopped; FAIL if both cheques are stopped, the cleared one is stopped, or the check precedes the act incorrectly.
